_readme: Rename this file to clips.json to activate it. With no clips.json present
the game loads exactly as before, so this file is safe to leave here.
A rigging service returns ONE animation baked into ONE GLB, so a full move
set arrives as several files rather than one file with several clips. This
maps those files onto the game's states. The FILENAME decides the slot, so
these never go through the clip-name matching table.
Keys are the character basenames from ASSETS.fighters / ASSETS.assists:
p1 p2 p3 p4   the four fighters
s1 s2         the two summons
Per character, both fields are optional:
model   a rigged replacement for that character's mesh. Tried BEFORE
the authored pN.fbx, so the rigged output becomes the fighter.
clips   slot -> file. Valid slots: IDLE WALK JUMP PUNCH KICK BLOCK
HITSTUN KO
Partial sets are fine and expected. A state with no clip stays on the
procedural bone driver, so buying two clips gives you those two and leaves
everything else animating as it does today.
Values are resolved against assets/models/ unless they contain a slash or
start with http, so a remote URL works too.
Clips are retargeted by bone name before binding: a clip authored against
'Hips' or 'arm_r' will still drive a model whose bones are called
'mixamorigHips' and 'mixamorigRightArm'. A clip that matches too little of
the skeleton is REJECTED rather than bound silently, and the dev panel (H)
reports it as 'N unbindable' — check the MODELS row after loading.
